recipes.name: Caramel Apple Biscuits
ingredients: 1 tablespoon (14g) light brown sugar or dark brown sugar, packed
1 tablespoon (21g) boiled cider or maple syrup
2 cups (227g) King Arthur Unbleached Self-Rising Flour
1/4 cup (53g) light brown sugar or dark brown sugar, packed
2 tablespoons (43g) boiled cider or 2 tablespoons (36g) apple juice concentrate
2 cups (227g) peeled, sliced cooking apples (Granny Smiths, Braeburn, Galas)
sentences: To make the caramel: Place the sugar in a 2-quart heavy saucepan (preferably light colored).
Bring to a boil, and cook without stirring until the sugar begins to caramelize (become light to medium brown), which will take about 8 minutes.
If using a thermometer, cook the sugar until it's between 350°F and 360°F.
To make the biscuits: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Turn the dough out onto a piece of parchment paper, pat it into a 6" to 6 1/2" circle (about 3/4" thick), and cut into circles with a 2" cutter.
Pile any scraps on top of each other, fold twice to bring them together, and cut the remaining dough; you should get 8 to 10 biscuits.
Place the biscuits on a baking sheet, leaving 2" between them.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until they're light golden brown.
Cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally, then add the caramel sauce and boiled cider.
Cook for 1 minute more, then remove from the heat.
To assemble: Split the biscuits, and spoon 5 to 6 apple slices over the bottom half of each.

recipes.name: Gluten-Free Vanilla Cake Pan Cake
yield: one 8” square cake or 9” round cake
ingredients: 2 cups (240g) King Arthur Gluten-Free Measure for Measure Flour
4 1/2 teaspoons (21g) cider vinegar or white vinegar
1 tablespoon (14g) King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract
4 tablespoons (57g) butter or vegan butter, at room temperature
2 1/2 cups (283g) confectioners' sugar, sifted if lumpy
1/2 teaspoon King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract
sentences: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Lightly grease an 8” square or 9” round pan that’s at least 2” deep.
Bake the cake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the top feels set, the edges are beginning to pull away from the sides of the pan, and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Add the vanilla and 1 tablespoon of the water, beating to incorporate.

recipes.name: Golden Cheese Bread
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups (180g) King Arthur Unbleached Bread Flour
1 1/2 cups (170g) King Arthur Golden Wheat Flour
1/4 cup (28g) King Arthur Baker's Special Dry Milk or nonfat dry milk
1/3 cup (39g) King Arthur Better Cheddar Cheese Powder, optional for enhanced cheese flavor
4 teaspoons King Arthur Pizza Dough Flavor, optional for enhanced flavor
3/4 teaspoon onion powder, optional for enhanced flavor
1 1/3 cups (152g) shredded cheese: pizza blend, mozzarella, cheddar, or the cheese of your choice
sentences: Place the dough in a lightly greased bowl, cover it, and let it rise until very puffy (though not necessarily doubled), about 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Gently deflate the dough, and divide it into small (about 1") pieces.
Dividing the dough into half, then each piece into half again, etc. works well; you want to end up with 64 pieces of dough, more or less.
Lightly grease a 9" x 5" loaf pan, and line the bottom with parchment or foil.
Place 16 dough pieces in the bottom of the pan, putting them close together.
Sprinkle with 1/3 cup of the shredded cheese.
Place another 16 pieces of dough atop the first layer.
Sprinkle with 1/3 cup cheese, and drizzle or brush with some more of the melted butter.
Cover the pan, and let the bread rise for 30 to 60 minutes, until it's slightly crowned over the rim of the pan.
Towards the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 350°F.
Bake the bread for 20 minutes.
Cover it lightly with aluminum foil and bake for an additional 15 to 20 minutes, until a digital thermometer inserted into the center registers about 190°F.
Wait 2 minutes, and turn it out of the pan onto a baking sheet.
Carefully turn it right side up, sprinkle the top with the remaining 1/3 cup cheese, and return it to the oven for about 2 minutes, just until the cheese softens and starts to melt.

recipes.name: Grilled Garlic Knots
ingredients: 1 large head (38g) garlic, about 6 to 7 cloves, intact
2 1/2 cups plus 1 tablespoon (300g) King Arthur ‘00’ Pizza Flour*
1 1/2 teaspoons instant yeast or active dry yeast
1 teaspoon olive oil, for brushing on the dough
2/3 cup (75g) mozzarella cheese, grated, low-moisture preferred
2 tablespoons (20g) King Arthur Semolina Flour or yellow cornmeal
1/4 cup (13g) parsley or basil, finely minced
sentences: Microwave the garlic for 3 to 5 minutes at 50% power, until the cloves are soft and cooked through.
This should take 30 to 45 seconds in a mixer using the flat beater; or about 1 minute by hand, using a spoon or spatula.
After 30 minutes, uncover the bowl and use a bowl scraper or your wet hand to grab a section of dough from one side, lift it up, and press it down to the middle to seal.
Repeat three more times, turning the bowl 90° each time.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rest, undisturbed, for at least 30 minutes or for up to three hours.
To shape the rolls: Place the dough on a lightly floured surface and roll it into an 18" x 8" rectangle, roughly 1/4” thick.
To add the filling: Brush the oil evenly over the dough, covering all but a 1/2” strip along one long side.
Sprinkle on the cheeses and Pizza Seasoning, leaving the same 1/2" strip uncovered.
Cut the log into eighteen 1” slices.
Sprinkle a light layer of semolina or cornmeal (about 1 tablespoon) onto a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Thread the rolls onto 10” to 12” metal or bamboo skewers, poking them through the center of their sidewalls.
Use three rolls per skewer, leaving about 1 1/2" of empty space between each.
Set the skewers on the prepared baking sheet and allow the rolls to rest, covered, for 20 to 30 minutes while you preheat the grill to 350°F.
To grill the rolls: Lay the skewers on the preheated grill, cooking the rolls for 4 to 5 minutes per side.
Grill until well baked; a digital thermometer will read 190°F when inserted into the center of a fully cooked roll.
Reheat leftover rolls, well-wrapped in foil, for about 5 minutes in a toaster oven or your oven set to 300°F before enjoying.

recipes.name: Irish Raisin Bread
ingredients: 1 cup (113g) King Arthur Golden Wheat Flour
2 cups (240g) King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
3 tablespoons (32g) potato flour or 1/3 cup (32g) dried potato flakes (instant mashed potatoes)
3 tablespoons (50g) light brown sugar or dark brown sugar, packed
1 cup (170g) golden raisins, dark raisins, or a combination; or currants
sentences: Cover the bowl, and let the preferment rest overnight (or for up to 20 hours or so), at room temperature; it doesn't need to be placed somewhere warm.
Place the dough in a greased bowl or greased 8-cup measure, cover it, and let it rise for 60 to 90 minutes, until it's noticeably puffy though not necessarily doubled in bulk.
If you have time, let the dough rest for 20 to 30 minutes; this short rest will make it easier to shape.
Shape the dough into a log, and place it into a lightly greased 8 1/2" x 4 1/2" loaf pan.
Allow the dough to rise until it's crowned about 1/2" to 3/4" over the rim of the pan, 60 to 90 minutes.
Towards the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 350°F.
Bake the bread for 20 minutes.
Tent it loosely with aluminum foil, and bake for an additional 20 to 25 minutes, until it's golden brown all over.
If it wobbles or feels too soft, return it to the oven for 5 to 10 minutes.
Wrap airtight, and store at room temperature for up to 5 days; for longer storage, wrap well and freeze.

recipes.name: Organic Whole Grain Banana Bread
ingredients: 2 cups (454g) thoroughly mashed banana, about 4 or 5 medium bananas
1 cup (213g) light brown sugar or dark brown sugar, firmly packed
1 teaspoon King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract
1 cup (120g) King Arthur Organic All-Purpose Flour
1 cup (113g) King Arthur Golden Wheat Flour
1/2 cup (57g) chopped walnuts, toasted if desired; optional*
sentences: Preheat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center position.
Lightly grease a 9" x 5" loaf pan; if your pan is glass or stoneware, reduce the oven temperature to 325°F.

Bake the bread for about 60 to 75 minutes, until the bread feels set on the top, and a paring knife (or other thin knife) inserted into the center comes out clean, or with just a few moist crumbs (but no wet batter).
If you have a digital thermometer, the bread's temperature at the center should register about 205°F.
If the bread appears to be browning too quickly, tent it with aluminum foil for the final 15 to 20 minutes of baking.
Note: If baking in a glass or stoneware pan, increase the baking time by 10 to 15 minutes.
Cool it in the pan for 15 minutes, then loosen the edges, and turn it out of the pan onto a rack to cool completely.

recipes.name: Sourdough Doughnuts
ingredients: 1/3 cup (40g) King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
1/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons (85g) milk, whole preferred
2 2/3 cups (320g) King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
1 teaspoon King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract
sentences: Place the saucepan over medium heat and cook, stirring regularly, until the mixture is thickened, paste-like, and the spoon or spatula leaves lines on the bottom of the pan, 2 to 3 minutes.
Mix on low speed to bring the dough together, about 1 minute, then pause to scrape the bowl.
Next, mix on medium speed until the dough is smooth, sticky, and shiny, 2 to 3 minutes.
With the mixer running, add the butter 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing until fully incorporated after each addition.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise at room temperature for 1 hour, or until slightly puffy but not doubled in volume.
Transfer the bowl to the refrigerator for at least 1 hour and up to 24 hours.
While the dough is chilling, gather ten parchment squares or cut ten 4" squares of parchment.
Use a rolling pin or your hands to gently flatten the dough to an even 1/2" thickness.
Use a floured 3 1/2" round cutter to cut out doughnuts, then use a floured 1 1/2" round cutter to cut a hole out of the center of each.
Gather the dough scraps and gently reroll them to an even 1/2" thickness.
Cut out more doughnuts and doughnut holes until you have 9 doughnuts and 9 doughnut holes.
Let the doughnuts rise at room temperature for 15 to 30 minutes, or until they are slightly puffy and hold an indentation when gently pressed with a floured fingertip.
To fry the doughnuts: Toward the end of the rising time, heat the oil to 325°F in a large, heavy pot.

Fry 3 doughnuts at a time, using the parchment squares to carefully invert each doughnut into the hot oil (parchment-side up); the parchment should quickly release — use tongs to dispose of it. (If it doesn’t release, don’t worry: It will when you flip the doughnuts.) Cook the doughnuts for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, until they’re brown on the bottom.
Using a slotted spoon, turn the doughnuts over and cook until brown on the other side, another 1 1/2 to 2 minutes.
Adjust the heat as necessary to keep the oil between 325°F and 350°F.
Fry the doughnut holes in a single batch, gently stirring and turning them constantly with the slotted spoon for about 3 to 4 minutes, until brown all over.
Dip the cooled doughnuts and doughnut holes into the glaze, fully coating one side, then return them to the rack to let the glaze set, about 1 minute.
Leftover doughnuts can be stored in a paper bag at room temperature for up to 1 day.
They taste best when reheated in the microwave for 10 seconds.

recipes.name: Strawberry Cream Meringue Pie
ingredients: one batch Classic Single Pie Crust, prepared
1 tablespoon (11g) Instant Clearjel, optional; for improved thickening
6 cups (999g) strawberries, washed, trimmed of their leaves, and sliced
6 tablespoons (42g) King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
3 large egg yolks, (reserve the whites for the topping)
sentences: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
To shape the crust: Roll the pastry into a 12" circle and place it in a 9" pie pan that's at least 1 1/2" deep.
Bake the crust for 18 minutes, until set but not browned.
Let sit for 10 minutes to allow the strawberries to release their juice, then cook the fruit over medium heat until the butter is melted.
Reduce the oven temperature to 350°F and bake the pie for 20 minutes.
Microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring after each, until the mixture thickens and becomes translucent.
Return the pie to the oven and bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until the meringue is lightly browned.

recipes.name: White Breakfast Bread
ingredients: 1 1/2 tablespoons King Arthur Baker's Special Dry Milk or nonfat dry milk
3 3/4 cups (450g) King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
sentences: Check the dough's consistency about 7 minutes after the kneading cycle begins, adding additional water or flour to form a smooth, soft ball of dough.

recipes.name: Whole Wheat Pizza Crust
ingredients: 3 cups (340g) King Arthur Golden Wheat Flour
3/4 cup to 7/8 cup (170g to 198g) lukewarm water
sentences: Cover and let rest for 30 minutes, to give the whole wheat flour time to absorb the liquid.
After 30 minutes, check the dough's consistency.
If it seems stiff, add 2 more tablespoons of water; then mix and knead until the dough is smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
Cover and let the dough rest at room temperature for 30 minutes, then refrigerate overnight, or as long as 18 hours.
Remove the dough from the refrigerator and pat it into a lightly greased half-sheet pan (18" x 13").
Cover with greased plastic and let rise for about 2 hours, until very puffy.
Toward the end of the rise time, preheat the oven to 450°F.
Bake for 8 minutes, then remove from the oven and top with cheese.
Return to the oven and bake for 6 to 8 minutes more, until the cheese is melted and the crust is browned.
Remove from the oven, and let rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Store leftover pizza covered and refrigerated for up to 5 days.
